prior_failures.evidence: "How an answer is tied to its parts. Each choice that Ask the setup questions (fn-setup-questions) offers is built from one named place in Phoenix memory:" "An answer that names no place (for example database no) selects no block. A part that two selected blocks both need is built once and names both answers that selected it," "Words this page uses. Phoenix memory is the one shared memory on a machine"
prior_failures.fix: Split the Rules & behavior bullet that starts "How an answer is tied to its parts." into separate bullets, one rule each: (1) each choice maps to one named place in Phoenix memory (a standards folder, a domain shelf, or one part of a shelf), which is the block's selection; (2) to build a block, initialize asks the memory tool for what the selection finds and keeps only the parts that speak to the answer; (3) an answer that names no place (database no) selects no block; (4) a part two blocks both need is built once and names both answers, so dropping one answer keeps it for the other; (5) our default: a part is cut along the file's own sections and a section is kept when it speaks to the answer. Likewise split the "Words this page uses." bullet into one bullet per term (Phoenix memory, Garura memory, memory block, part, product profile).
